why: The statement quantifies over all pairs (k,ℓ), so each settled pair is a case, not the whole. Pre-snapshot: Kára–Pór–Wood (k≤4) and Abel et al. (k=5) are journal-accepted cases; Addario-Berry (5,4) is secondary-sourced and unreviewed; Pfender, Hujter–Kisfaludi-Bak (chromatic), Pór–Wood (infinite sets) and Leuchtner et al. (visible islands) answer changed questions; Barát et al. only moves the threshold for an already-settled k=5. Post-snapshot: Bonnet settles (6,4) and by his own account GPT-5.6 Sol Pro produced the detailed proof with the author checking and simplifying — generated. Cambie reproves (6,4) with an AI-credited 'assistance' phrase that does not say which steps the model produced — assisted, with doubtful credibility over the unexplained threshold gap. Bhattacharya et al. give K₇∖e (not a (k,ℓ) pair) but their appendix explicitly proves (6,4), so case; GPT-6 Astra produced initial proofs of Theorems 1.1/1.3 which the humans revised — assisted rather than generated, a close call. Sarkar's results restrict to structured classes of point sets (on a fixed irreducible curve, etc.), read as a case; AI use was typesetting/search/proofreading only.
doubts: Sarkar could instead be read as a variant (structured hypotheses) rather than a case; either way it adds no AI. Cambie's arXiv comment 'a 2 page AI version was essentially reviewed by the author' suggests the AI may have generated the note, which would make it generated rather than assisted; the basis quote alone supports only assisted. Bhattacharya et al.'s role could be generated given 'produced the initial proofs'. All 2026 quotes come via summarising HTML fetches, not PDFs.
